author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: These parsers read Genesys Cloud CX audit events from the Audit API's asynchronous query. The example bridge in bridges/genesys-cloud-audit-logs polls them and posts them to HTTP Ingest. AuthUser and UserSamlAuthentication events go to Auth, and every other event goes to CloudAudit.
notes:
Setup:
- The example bridge in bridges/genesys-cloud-audit-logs polls Genesys Cloud CX audit events from the Audit API's asynchronous query and posts them to HTTP Ingest.
- Use an OAuth client with the Client Credentials grant and a role with only Audits > Audit > View.
- The bridge uses the asynchronous query because the real-time one has no successful sign-ins and leaves some services out.
- The bridge puts "genesys_record": "audit" first.

Field mapping:
- AuthUser and UserSamlAuthentication events go to Auth: Authenticate is a sign-in, AuthenticationFailed a failed one (Genesys gives no reason, so the failure category is OTHER_ERROR), ChangePassword a password change and SingleLogout a SAML sign-out.
- The target user is the entity's name, since a SAML event's user is empty, then the user's name or ID.
- Every other event goes to CloudAudit with the action as the event name, the service as the event type, the entity as the resource and the OAuth client as the access key.
- The first two property changes go to the request parameters (new values) and the additional data (old values).
- Read, View, Download and Export are read-only data events.
- The source address is the first entry of remoteIp, which Genesys describes as the systems that originated or handled the request.
- Each event's id is the event ID.

Made up in the samples:
- Samples follow the AuditLogMessage shape in Genesys's API reference and Sample Usage page, with entity types and actions from its Action Catalog and made-up values.
- Genesys publishes no sign-in example, so the sign-in records follow the shape of a SAML sign-out record posted on the Genesys community, with message codes made up in its style.

Testing:
- Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-22 (147 of 147 fields matched the emulator in each of 3 runs), and the parent's confirm string picked the same records there.
- Each child also passed Run Test as a separate parser under its parent (147 of 147 fields, each line taken in 5 of 5 runs).
- No built-in parser claimed these records in 3 runs.
